decisions.reason: The inverse identity is true by the imported def-natural-logarithm, but F2 and its quoted interfaces omit that definition. This is a local citation defect, not a false convergence claim. Replaced the inverse-log estimate by exp(u)=sum u^j/j! <= (1-u)^(-1)<4/3 using the existing exponential-series definition and geometric-series supplier. Also corrected the strict bound at K=r=0 and supplied an explicit uniform geometric tail.

The general H_Lambda was ambiguous between two supplier energies, although the displayed Ising sum already used free boundaries. Defined H_Lambda=H_Lambda^free explicitly for nonempty finite regions, with exterior-labelled conditional partitions separate. Specified translation invariance for stationary laws. The Gaussian substitution, activity units, SI conversion, and reference-action qualifications remain valid.

The definition expressly calls its finite Gibbs formula a candidate. The justified_by lemma assumes that formula and the finite-alphabet interaction data, then proves finite positive normalization in 1.1, measurability/properness in 2.2 and consistency by a finite sum in 2.1. It does not assume those kernel conclusions. This is exactly the schema-permitted definition-to-justification dependency pattern, not circular reasoning.

The statement and proof correctly construct an unconditioned stationary two-sided Markov law: positivity gives r, Tr=lambda r gives stochastic Q, symmetry gives invariant pi, and endpoint summation gives consistent block marginals and their unique extension under AC_omega. The title could suggest endpoint conditioning, so renamed it to describe the actual stationary law. No mathematical claim or proof changed.

Step 1.1 applied the parity supplier outside its n>=1 hypotheses and left n=0 without a containment/boundary proof. Preserved the full nonnegative integer domain explicitly and proved the n=0 case: the only disagreement cycle is the unit square about the lone negative spin, with inside {0} and exactly its four boundary bonds. The existing involutive flip then changes precisely |gamma| bonds, lowers energy by 2J|gamma| and gives the injection weight bound. This is a logical hypothesis gap, not a counterexample to the claimed inequality.

A1 attributed extension to the axiom-definition item; the existing F1 correctly supplies probability compactness and extension, so the proof already had the necessary theorem. Restated A1 as AC_omega itself and assigned the measure conclusions to F1. Checked cylinder locality passes finite kernel identities to subsequential limits, equality on generating cylinders gives DLR, and convexity/closedness follow from those same linear local identities.

F1 overstated its direct theorem by attributing sequential compactness to its stated closedness conclusion. Added the existing ambient probability-compactness lemma as a direct supplier and F2, then used its subsequence theorem plus DLR closedness separately. Wrote translation covariance as an explicit kernel identity; averaging preserves DLR, the cube symmetric-difference ratio tends to zero, and the cylinder limit is invariant under each fixed lattice translation. The mathematical conclusion and AC_omega scope are unchanged.

F4 dropped the stationary-state supplier nonemptiness hypothesis, leaving attainment in 3.1 without an explicit licensed existence premise. Added the existing kernel-consistency and DLR-existence results as direct prerequisites and stated their hypotheses/conclusions before applying averaging. Checked the entropy upper bound and equality argument; defined the boundary layer and an explicit crossing-term constant C=sum |S_r| norm(Phi_r), giving relative entropy at most 2 beta C |boundary|=o(volume). All original variational claims, including no converse, are preserved.

The pressure value was mathematically correct but its physical example omitted the dimensionless per-site normalization. Specified p=lim N^(-1) log Z_N with the explicit periodic dimensionless partition and N>=2; no physical-volume conversion is being asserted. Kept zero field in Given and clarified that endpoint convergence belongs to the DLR uniqueness theorem, while the transfer-matrix lemma supplies the stationary law. The corrected series supplier retains exactly the example range 0<K<1/2.

A1 did wrongly attribute existence to the AC_omega definition. The stronger judge claim that no existence premise was available is false: F2 already invokes the Dobrushin result, whose proof 5.1 uses the DLR existence theorem. Corrected A1 to state the axiom and cite that existence theorem directly, added its dependency, and separated existence from uniqueness in 2.1. The finite interaction-list construction preserves unordered-pair normalization and the uniform one-site radius, and the influence bound gives the required strict row sum.

F3 omitted essential conditions in its local restatement, but the original Statement and proof 1.3 already confined the application to the stated low-temperature model. Made AC_omega, d=2, nearest-neighbor interactions, J>0, beta>0, h=0 and beta J>=2 explicit in F3 and 1.3. The original three conditional predictions are preserved. Corrected physical_scope to include the general finite-range d-dimensional uniqueness branch already claimed in Statement (ii). The cusp follows from the supplier secant inequalities, and no empirical premise or measured critical point is introduced.

The original coexistence claim omitted h=0 and was false for its stated scope: if h>4J, every square-lattice one-site conditional mean is at least tanh(beta(h-4J))>0, so no DLR state can have negative one-site magnetization. Made the constant field energy explicit, retained the sufficient high-temperature uniqueness condition for every finite h, and imposed h=0 only on the K>=2 coexistence branch in Example, Given, F2, verification and physical_scope. All conclusions remain conditional predictions, with neither empirical transition data nor an exact critical point asserted.
